questions.question: What is the Steam Point on the Fahrenheit scale?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**212° F.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Steam Point on the Fahrenheit scale is **212° F.**
 
• The temperature at which water vapour condenses at a pressure of one atmosphere, is represented by **100°C and 212°F.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Celsius scale:

 
 
• In this scale, a lower fixed point (ice point) is designated as 0° and the upper fixed point (steam point) is designated as 100°.
 
• The temperature measured on this scale was all in degrees Celsius (° C).
 
 
 
• Fahrenheit scale:
 
 
• On this scale of the temperature scale, the melting point of ice is considered to be 32° F and the boiling point of water is 212° F.
 
• The change in temperature of 1° F corresponds to a change of less than 1° C on the Celsius scale.
 
 
 
• Kelvin scale:
 
 
• We also know the Kelvin temperature scale as the thermodynamic scale. 
 
• On the Kelvin scale, the boiling point of the water is considered to be 373.15 K and its freezing point is 273.15 K.

questions.question: The Sun is visible to us approximately ______ minutes before the sunrise because of atmospheric refraction.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__2.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sun is visible to us **about 2 minutes before the actual sunrise** and **about 2 minutes after the actual sunset**.
 
• The sun is visible **before the actual sunrise** and **after the actual sunset**, because of **atmospheric refraction**.
 
 
• With **altitude, the density and hence refractive index of air-layer decreases**.
 
• The light rays starting from the sun travel from rarer to denser layers. They bend more and more towards the normal. To an observer on the earth, light rays appear to come from an Apparent position. The sun which is actually in its original position below the horizon appears in an apparent position above the horizon. Thus the sun appears to rise early by about two minutes and for the same reason, it appears to set late by about two minutes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **This increases the length of the day by about four minutes**.

questions.question: Which force causes the trade winds of the southern hemisphere to start blowing from southwest to northeast in India after crossing the equator?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coriolis force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Coriolis force is an apparent force that is observed due to the rotation of the Earth.**
 
• **It deflects the path of moving objects, such as winds and ocean currents, to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere.**
 
• In the southern hemisphere, the trade winds start blowing from the southeast towards the equator due to the Coriolis force.
 
• As the winds cross the equator, they are deflected to the right by the Coriolis force, causing them to blow towards the northeast in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gravitational force**

 
 
• It is the force of attraction between two masses, such as the Earth and objects on its surface.
 
• **It is responsible for keeping objects, such as the Moon, in orbit around the Earth and for causing tides.**
 
 
 
• **Magnetic force**
 
 
• **It is the force exerted by magnets and magnetic fields.**
 
• It is responsible for the behavior of compass needles and the Earth's magnetic field, which protects the planet from harmful solar radiation.
 
 
 
• **Centrifugal force**
 
 
• **It is the apparent force that is observed due to the rotation of a rotating frame of reference.**
 
• It is often used to explain the behavior of objects in circular motion, but it is not a real force as it is not caused by an interaction between two objects.

questions.question: A force acts on an object which is free to move. If we know the magnitude of the force and the mass of the object then Newton’s second law of motion enables us to determine the object’s ________.
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• The second law states that the acceleration of an object is dependent upon two variables - the net force acting upon the object and the mass of the object.
 
• The acceleration in a body is due to an unbalanced force, this can be explained by the first two of Newton's laws of motion
 
• According to Newton's first law of motion, an object continues to be in a state of rest or of motion until an external and unbalanced force is applied to it
 
• According to Newton's second law of motion, the force is equal to the change in the rate of momentum, that is,

Initial momentum = mu

Final momentum = mv

Force = Change in the rate of momentum given by:

F=(mv-mu)/(t)=m((v-u)/(t))=ma

Here, m is the mass of the object

u is the initial velocity is the velocity after time t

a is the acceleration

Therefore, **acceleration in the body is due to the unbalanced force.**__

questions.question: A set of equations involving electric and magnetic fields, and their sources, the charge and current densities are known as ______ equations.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maxwell’s**__.

__
 
• **Maxwell formulated** a set of equations involving electric and magnetic fields, and their sources, the charge and current densities.
 
• We have so far established that the total flux of electric field out of a closed surface is just the total enclosed charge multiplied by 1/ε₀

 **∫E⋅dA = q/ε₀**, It represents completely covering the surface with a large number of tiny patches having areas dA.,**ε₀ = Vacuum permittivity**.
 
• **The electric field at a point situated at a distance d from a straight charged conductor is inversely proportional to d**.
 
• **A field line and an equipotential surface are always at 90°**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
 

 Newton’s Equations
 
 
 
• 1st law: An object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion stays in motion with the same speed and the same direction unless acted upon by an unbalanced force.
 
 
• Newton’s first law of motion, which is sometimes called the law of inertia, explains that an object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion remains in motion with the same velocity unless acted upon by an external force.
 
 
 
• 2nd law: the acceleration of an object is dependent upon two variables - the net force acting upon the object and the mass of the object.
 
 
• The acceleration of an object depends directly upon the net force acting upon the object, and inversely upon the mass of the object.
 
• Newton's 2nd law of motion says the rate change of momentum is called force.
 
 
 
• 3rd law: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
• Newton's law of universal gravitation: The attractive force between two objects (F) is equal to G times the product of their masses (m1, m2) divided by the square of the distance between them (r).

 F = G(m1m2/r2)
 
 
 
 

 Bohr's equation
 
 
 
• The great Danish physicist Niels Bohr made immediate use of Rutherford’s planetary model of the atom.
 
• Bohr’s theory explained the atomic spectrum of hydrogen and established new and broadly applicable principles in quantum mechanics.
 
• The observed hydrogen-spectrum wavelengths can be calculated using the following formula:

 1/λ=R(1/nf²−1/nᵢ²), where λ is the wavelength of the emitted EM radiation and R is the Rydberg constant, determined by the experiment to be R = 1.097 × 107 / m (or m−¹). The constant nf is a positive integer associated with a specific series.
 
 
 
 

 Einstein’s equation
 
 
 
• Einstein's theory of special relativity shows that matter (as mass) and energy can be converted into each other according to the famous equation E = mc², where E is energy, m is mass, and c is the speed of light.

__

questions.question: When the speed of a moving body doubles, then what is the change in its kinetic energy?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **Option 2, i.e. ****__It gets quadrupled__**.

__
 
• When the speed of a moving body double, then its kinetic energy** get quadrupled.**
 
• **Kinetic energy** is the force of movement. An object with motion-whether vertical or horizontal-has kinetic energy.
 
• **Kinetic Energy = 1/2 × (mv)²**
 
• **New Velocity V' = 2v**
 
• **So, new Kinetic Energy = 1/2 × (m × 2v)²**
 
• **There, New Kinetic Energy = 2 (mv)² = 4 × Kinetic Energy__**

questions.question: What is the name of the phenomenon by which light splits into its component colours upon passing through a prism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dispersion**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** phenomenon where white light splits into its component colors when passing through a prism is called dispersion. **
 
• White light is made up of **seven bands of colors**, each with a different wavelength. 
 
• When white light passes through a medium, each color travels at a different speed and has a different angle of refraction. 
 
• **This causes the light to split, or disperse. **
 
• **For example**, when light travels from air into water, it slows down, causing it to continue to travel at a different angle or direction. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diffraction**

 
 
• When a **wave passes through a small opening or around a barrier, it bends and spreads out.**
 
• This can be demonstrated by placing obstacles in a ripple tank and observing the path of the water waves. 
 
 
 
• **Reflection**
 
 
• When **light rays bounce off a surface**.
 
• The law of reflection states that the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence. 
 
 
 
• **Refraction**
 
 
• When a **ray of light passes from one medium to another, it changes direction at the boundary.**
 
• The path of the light depends on the density of the materials.
 
• **For example, l**ight bends toward the normal when it travels from a less dense medium to a denser medium. 
 
 
 
• **Rainbows are formed by a combination of refraction, dispersion, and total internal reflection.**
 
• When **sunlight passes through water droplets in the atmosphere, the droplets act like prisms, refracting and dispersing the light, reflecting it internally, and then refracting it again when it exits the droplet**.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding inertia?

I. Inertia is the natural tendency of an object to resist a change in its state of motion or of rest.

II. The mass of an object is a measure of its inertia.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton's first law of motion** 

 
 
• **States that "An object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion stays in motion with the same speed and in the same direction unless acted upon by an unbalanced force."**
 
• Objects tend to "keep on doing what they're doing."
 
• In fact, it is the natural tendency of objects to resist changes in their state of motion.
 
• **This tendency to resist changes in their state of motion is described as inertia.**
 
 

**​(Hence statement I is correct)**

 
• **Inertia:**

 
 
• The resistance an object has to a change in its state of motion.
 
• All objects resist changes in their state of motion. All objects have this tendency - they have inertia.
 
• **The tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of motion varies with mass.**
 
 

**​((Hence statement II is correct))**

 
• Mass is that quantity that is solely dependent upon the inertia of an object.
 
• The more inertia that an object has, the more mass that it has.
 
• A more massive object has a greater tendency to resist changes in its state of motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Laws of motion:**

 
 

 **Law of Motion**
 **Description**
 **Example**
 
 
 
 

 Newton's First Law
 An object at rest tends to stay at rest, and an object in motion tends to stay in motion with the same speed and direction unless acted upon by an external force.
 A book resting on a table will remain at rest until an external force, such as pushing it, is applied.
 
 

 Newton's Second Law
 The acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting on it and inversely proportional to its mass.
 If you push a small ball and a large ball with the same amount of force, the smaller ball will experience a larger acceleration due to its lower mass.
 
 

 Newton's Third Law
 For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 When you swim, the action of pushing the water backwards with your arms and legs creates an equal and opposite reaction that propels you forward.

questions.question: In diffraction of white light by a prism, which colour of light from VIBGYOR will be bent most?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Violet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When white light travels through a prism, **violet light** bends the most, while red light bends the least.
 
• This occurs because violet light possesses the shortest wavelength among the seven colors in white light, while red light has the longest.
 
• **The dispersion of light,** which separates white light into its constituent colors, is responsible for this phenomenon.
 
• The refractive index of the medium is highest for violet light and lowest for red light. Refraction occurs as light enters the prism at an angle, with the degree of deviation varying based on wavelength. Consequently, different colors deviate at distinct angles, resulting in their separation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Violet light**, with the shortest wavelength among the seven constituent colors of light, experiences the greatest deviation, while red light, with the longest wavelength, undergoes the least. 
 
• Thus, the order of colors, commonly remembered as **VIBGYOR (violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red),** reflects this sequence based on their respective wavelengths and degrees of deviation.

questions.question: What is the total charge of an electric dipole?

• An electric dipole is pair of equal and opposite charges separated by a distance of 2a, the midpoint of locations -q and + q is called the centre of the dipole.
 
• The total charge of an electric dipole is **zero.**
 
• Electric dipole moment is the product of the magnitude of one charge multiplied by the distance of separation between the charge and is given by

⇒ P = 2a × q

Where P = dipole moment, 2a = Distance between the charge, and q = Charge

**Ductility**

__
 
• The property of metals due to which they can be drawn into thin wires is called ductility.
 
• Ductility is the ability of a material to deform under tensile stress, which allows it to be drawn into a wire or stretched into a thin sheet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Malleability is the property of metals through which metals can be converted into thin sheets.

 
 
• Examples of malleability: copper, silver, and lead.
 
• Gold and silver are highly malleable.
 
 
 
• **Conductivity**
 
 
• Conductivity is the measure of the ease at which an electric charge or heat can pass through a material.
 
• 
 
The material which has high conductivity is called conductor and which has very low conductivity is called non-conductor.

 
 
• 
 
Metal has high conductivity and non-metal has very low conductivity.

 
 
• Electrical conductivity is also known as specific conductance.
 
• It is denoted by the symbol σ and has SI units of Siemens per meter (S/m) or Ω-1m-1.
 
 
 
• **​Refinement**

questions.question: Identify the INCORRECT pair regarding motion and their examples?

options.text: Translatory motion – A ball falling from the cliff
Periodic motion – Hands of a clock
Oscillatory motion – Earth moving around the sun
Rotatory motion – blades of a fan

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oscillatory motion – Earth moving around the sun**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Oscillatory motion refers to the to-and-fro motion of an object about a mean position.
 
• The Earth moving around the sun is an example of circular motion, not oscillatory motion.
 
• In oscillatory motion, an object moves back and forth within a certain range.
 
• Examples of oscillatory motion include the motion of a pendulum and the vibrations of a spring.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Translatory Motion**

 
 
• In translatory motion, all parts of an object move the same distance in a given time.
 
• Examples include a car moving on a road and a ball falling from a cliff.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Motion**
 
 
• Periodic motion is a type of motion that repeats itself at regular time intervals.
 
• Examples include the hands of a clock and the motion of a swing.
 
 
 
• **Oscillatory Motion**
 
 
• Oscillatory motion is a type of periodic motion where an object moves back and forth about a mean position.
 
• Examples include the motion of a pendulum and the vibrations of a guitar string.
 
 
 
• **Rotatory Motion**
 
 
• Rotatory motion occurs when an object rotates around a fixed axis.
 
• Examples include the blades of a fan and the rotation of the Earth on its axis.
 
 
 
• **Circular Motion**
 
 
• Circular motion is a movement of an object along the circumference of a circle or rotation along a circular path.
 
• Examples include the Earth moving around the sun and a satellite orbiting the Earth.

questions.question: Which of the following is dimensionless?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Longitudinal strain.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• The powers to which fundamental quantities must be raised in order to express the given physical quantity are called its dimensions.
 
• A quantity without dimension will usually be a ratio of two quantities with similar dimensions and, hence, cancel out.
 
• Thus, they will have no units.

EXPLANATION__:

 
• **Longitudinal stress:**

 
 
• Longitudinal stress is the stress which acts along the length and its unit is **N/m² or Pascal.**
 
 
 
• **Shear stress: **
 
 
• **​**If the deforming force acts tangentially to the surface of the body, It produces a change in the shape of the body.
 
• This tangential force applied per unit area is called shear stress.
 
• Its unit is ** N/mm2 or MPa. **
 
 
 
• **Deforming force: **
 
 
• **​**Deforming Force An external force applied to a body that changes its size or shape or both is called deforming force.
 
• its unit is** N or kg-m/s².**
 
 
 
• **Longitudinal strain: **
 
 
• **​**The change in the length (ΔL) to the original length (L) of the body is known as longitudinal strain.
 
 

i.e., Longitudinal strain = frac{{{{Delta }}L}}{L}

 
• And since it is a ratio of two lengths, hence it is a **dimensionless **quantity.

questions.question: ______ is used in buildings and in manufacturing processes to prevent heat loss or heat gain.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Insulation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Insulation **is a general term used to describe material that creates barriers to the transmission of electricity, heat, moisture, shock, or sound between insulated surfaces of adjacent bodies. These materials could be insulating heat, cold, electricity, sound, or radiation.
 
• **To reduce heat loss or gain, insulation** is utilised in buildings and manufacturing processes.
 
• Although its major goal is to save money, it also allows for more precise temperature management and worker protection.
 
• It reduces rusting caused by moisture on cold surfaces. These materials are porous and have a lot of latent air cells.
 
• The building industry uses thermal insulation to decrease heat loss or gain through the home envelope (external walls, windows, roofs, foundation, etc.).
 
• Thermal insulation provides thermal comfort inside homes by maintaining a comfortable temperature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The flow of a fluid (liquid or gas) between locations of differing temperatures is known as **convection**.
 
• Heat energy is transferred through collisions between surrounding atoms or molecules in** the process of conduction**. 
 
• **Solidification, commonly known as freezing**, is a phase transition in which a liquid becomes a solid when its temperature is decreased below its freezing point.

questions.question: An image which can be obtained on a screen is called a ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**real image**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In optics, a **real image** is an image that is formed when rays converge at a specific point.
 
• They can be projected onto a screen or a photographic film.
 
• Real images can be produced by concave mirrors and converging** lenses, assuming the object is placed further from the mirror or lens than the focal point, and this image is inverted.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vector Image:**

 
 
• This refers to a type of digital graphic that uses mathematical formulas to render its design, instead of using pixel data like raster images.
 
• Because of this, vector images can be scaled to any size without loss of resolution. 
 
 
 
• **Virtual Image:**
 
 
• In the field of optics, a virtual image is an image formed when the outgoing rays from a point on the object always diverge.
 
• The image appears to be located at the point of apparent divergence.
 
• Because the rays never really converge, a virtual image cannot be projected onto a screen.
 
• Examples of virtual images include the image seen in a single plane mirror, the image seen through a magnifying glass, or the image seen in a camera viewfinder.
 
 
 
• **Spectral Image: **
 
 
• A spectral image is an image whose pixels contain information from across the electromagnetic spectrum.
 
• These images are captured by spectral imaging techniques which capture the entire spectrum in each pixel.
 
• These images are used for various purposes like remote sensing, astrophysics, etc.

questions.question: Which among the following is used as a reflector in search lights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Concave mirror.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Concave mirror is used as a reflector in search lights.
 
• Concave mirror: The mirrors curved inside on the reflecting side are called concave mirrors.
 
 
• These mirrors produce real as well as virtual images, inverted and erect, and magnified as well as the diminished image of the object.
 
• These are used in:
 
• reflecting telescope, 
 
• shaving mirrors, 
 
• ophthalmoscopes
 
• reflector for the headlight of a vehicle and
 
• searchlights.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Convex mirror: It is an outward curved mirror that produces a diminished image.

 
 
• Convex mirrors either diverge a parallel beam of light into all directions or gather light from all directions and produce a parallel beam out of it.
 
• Convex mirrors are used as rear view mirrors in vehicles, sunglasses, magnifying glasses.
 
• Convex mirrors are those which have the bulging side facing the light.
 
 
 
• **Concave lenses** are most commonly used to correct myopia which is also called near-sightedness. 
 
• **A plane mirror** has several different uses and applications, including periscope and kaleidoscope, automobiles, shaving mirrors, dentists' mirror, torch lights, solar cookers, and security-related purposes.

questions.question: What happens when two forces act in the opposite directions on an object?

options.text: The net force acting on the object is the difference between the two objects.
The net force acting on the object is the difference between the two forces.
The net force acting on the object is the total of the two forces.
The net force acting on the object is the sum of the two objects.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The net force acting on the object is the difference between the two forces.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When two forces act in opposite directions on an object, the net force is the difference between the two forces.
 
• The direction of the net force is in the direction of the larger force.
 
• If the forces are equal in magnitude but opposite in direction, they cancel each other out, resulting in a net force of zero.
 
• The concept of net force is crucial in understanding how forces influence the motion of objects according to Newton's Laws of Motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Force**

 
 
• A force is a push or pull upon an object resulting from its interaction with another object. Forces can cause objects to accelerate, decelerate, remain in place, or change shape.
 
• Forces are vector quantities, meaning they have both magnitude and direction.
 
• Forces can be categorized into contact forces (e.g., friction, tension) and action-at-a-distance forces (e.g., gravitational, electromagnetic).
 
 
 
• **Net Force**
 
 
• The net force is the vector sum of all the forces acting on an object.
 
• It determines the overall effect of all the forces on the motion of the object.
 
• According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, the net force acting on an object is equal to the mass of the object multiplied by its acceleration (F = ma).
 
 
 
• **Newton's Laws of Motion**
 
 
• **First Law (Law of Inertia)**: An object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by a net external force.
 
• **Second Law (Law of Acceleration)**: The acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting on it and inversely proportional to its mass (F = ma).
 
• **Third Law (Action and Reaction)**: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
 
 
• **Equilibrium**
 
 
• An object is in equilibrium when the net force acting on it is zero.
 
• In equilibrium, an object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion continues to move at a constant velocity.
 
• Equilibrium can be static (object at rest) or dynamic (object moving with constant velocity).

questions.question: Which of the following device is used to measure the distance travelled by the vehicle?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odometer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The device used to measure the distance traveled by a vehicle is called an odometer. 
 
• Odometers can be mechanical, electronic, or a combination of both, and they provide a reading of the total distance traveled by a vehicle.
 
• **Mechanical** Odometers: These use a series of gears and cogs to turn the reading on a dial as the vehicle moves.
 
• **Digital** Odometers: These are electronic and display the reading on a screen. They are often found in modern vehicles.

questions.question: ________ is a change of position.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Motion is the process of moving or being moved, as well as a change in the position of an item.**
 
• The term "**body in motion**" refers to when a body's location in relation to its **environment changes.**
 
• **Motion** is mathematically characterised in terms of **displacement, distance, velocity, acceleration, and speed** as well as the observer's frame of reference and the measurement of the change in the body's position with respect to that frame as time passes.
 
• **Kinematics** is the field of physics that studies forces and their effects on motion, while **dynamics** studies the motion of objects without regard to their source.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Speed**

 
 
• The distance travelled in relation to the time it took to travel that **distance** is how speed is defined. As **speed** simply has a direction and no **magnitude**, it is a **scalar** **quantity**.
 
 
 
• **Velocity**
 
 
• In **kinematics**, the area of classical mechanics that deals with the **motion** of bodies, **velocity** is a fundamental idea.** A physical vector quantity called velocity **must have both a **magnitude** and a direction in order to be defined.
 
 
 
• **Distance**
 
 
• **Distance** is the scientific term used to describe how far an object has moved. **A scalar quantity, distance.** **The International System of Units defines a metre as the distance unit.**
